summary: Postinstall executes an opaque 33MB Go binary that does not match shipped source or documented sizes
details: scripts/postinstall.mjs spawns vendor/gridgen-${process.platform}-${process.arch} at npm install time via spawnSync. The shipped native/gridgen.c is a ~10KB sudoku generator consistent only with the arm64 binaries; both x64 binaries are a bit-identical 33,648,788-byte stripped ELF Go executable (sha256 05b69666193e8fa719c37df22833bf36a120b15e2408a9ecd47e34f140a44420). The README misrepresents these files, listing them as 34,520 B and 13,160 B and claiming gridgen-darwin-x64 is Mach-O when it is in fact an ELF (which cannot execute on macOS, meaning only Linux x64 installers run the payload). The binary is not reproducible from the shipped C source, ships with no hash or signature verification, and the README's assertion that it 'reads no files, opens no sockets' cannot be verified from the opaque prebuilt bytes. On npm install on Linux x64 this executes attacker-controlled code with no consent path beyond the standard postinstall hook. The publisher scope @workoscalif also resembles the unrelated WorkOS auth vendor while the author (anas cherni, github.com/anascherni/sudoku) has no relation to WorkOS.
